description.narrative: Contract related to: EU support for Internal Marke - The Government remains committed to EU membership as its strategic goal. Serbia has opened 18 negotiation chapters of the acquis5 and two chapters (25 and 26) were provisionally closed so far. Serbia has a good level of preparation in the areas of company law, research and development and intellectual property law. It is moderately prepared in the areas of free movement of goods, right of establishment and freedom to provide services, competition policy, information society and media, enterprise and industrial policy, a s well as consumer and health protection6. Serbia has some level of preparation in agriculture and rural development.The Action is implementing the Government¿s strategic goals and strategic commitment to EU accession. The Action will contribute to strengthening of competitiveness and inclusive growth of Serbia by reaching two outcomes: Strengthening private sector development, trade, research and innovation and strengthening legislative and institutional capacities for fulfilling the requirements of EU membership in agriculture and rural development.Firstly, the Action will focus on improving market integrity and environment conducive to market operators by strengthening capacities of relevant stakeholders in the areas of Service Directive, market surveillance, intellectual property rights, state aid, competition policy and e-commerce. The Action will administer necessary policy and institutional adjustments market as well as market organisation and structural support in fisheries. It will improve enforcement of the agricultural land policies and animal health status in Serbia and surrounding countries.

title.narrative: OC7 Number of antitrust infringement and merger control proceedings closed by the CPC per year

description.narrative: This quantitative indicator tracks the annual number of antitrust infringement and merger control proceedings that are successfully closed by the Commission for Protection of Competition (CPC) in Serbia. Antitrust infringements involve actions that restrict free competition in the market, such as price fixing, market sharing, bid rigging, and abuse of market dominance. Merger control proceedings refer to regulatory reviews conducted by the CPC to assess and approve, conditionally approve, or reject mergers and acquisitions, ensuring they do not significantly impede effective competition. This indicator serves as a crucial metric for evaluating the effectiveness and efficiency of the CPC in upholding competitive market practices, which is vital for legal, administrative, and policy alignment with the European Unions competition law standards. The unit of measure is the total number of such proceedings concluded each year.Data for this indicator is sourced from the Commission for Protection of Competition Annual Progress Report. The baseline, established in 2021, is 233 closed proceedings. The target for 2026 is set at 260 proceedings, representing an expected increase of approximately 5%. This growth target is aimed at enhancing the CPCs capacity and responsiveness in handling complex competition cases, reflecting Serbias commitment to reinforcing its regulatory framework for competition and integrating more deeply into the EU Internal market.

title.narrative: OC5 Status of establishment of Point of Single Contact

description.narrative: This quantitative indicator assesses the progress in establishing the Point of Single Contact (PSC) in Serbia, a critical component under Key Area of Intervention 5. The PSC is an essential mechanism designed to facilitate the integration of Serbia into the EU Internal market by providing a centralized digital platform where businesses can access all necessary information and perform all administrative procedures required for operating in the EU. Currently, a dedicated website/digital platform is being designed and put in place to operationalize the PSC. This platform will centralize services, offering a streamlined, userfriendly interface that reduces administrative burdens and enhances transparency.The unit of measure for this indicator is the developmental status of the PSC, tracked from Not established to Fully implemented. According to the EU Serbia Report, as of June 2022 to June 2023, the baseline status of the PSC is Not established. The target for 2026 is for the PSC to be Fully implemented, indicating that it is expected to be operational and fully functional by the end of the intervention period. This setup aims to significantly enhance the ease of doing business in Serbia, aligning with EU standards and contributing to the broader objectives of market integration under the EUs regulatory framework.

description.narrative: This quantitative indicator monitors the annual number of decisions made by the Commission for State Aid Control (CSAC) in Serbia. Decisions adopted by the CSAC can include approvals, rejections, or requirements for modifications to state aid proposals, ensuring that all state aid measures are compliant with both national laws and EU regulations concerning competition and market fairness. These decisions are critical for evaluating the effectiveness of legal, administrative, and policy measures aimed at ensuring the alignment and integration of Serbian market practices with the EU Internal market, particularly in the area of state aid control.The unit of measurement for this indicator is the number of decisions adopted. Data for this indicator is sourced from the Commission for State Aid Control Reports, supplemented by information confirmed during consultations with partners. For 2022, the baseline value was established at 124 decisions. The target for 2026 is set at 136 decisions, reflecting an anticipated increase in CSAC activity, aligning with Key Area of Intervention 4 on State Aid. This increase underscores a proactive approach to monitoring and regulating state aid, essential for maintaining market competitiveness and compliance with EU standards.

title.narrative: OC8 Status of the Agreement on Conformity Assessment and Accreditation (ACCA) of industrial products

description.narrative: This qualitative indicator monitors the progress toward the signing of the Agreement on Conformity Assessment and Accreditation (ACCA) of industrial products between Serbia and the EU. An ACCA is an international agreement that facilitates trade by allowing products assessed and certified in one country to be accepted in another without the need for additional testing. It ensures that industrial products meet specific standards of quality and safety, which are aligned with international regulations, thus fostering smoother market integration.The unit of measure for this indicator is the status of the agreement, tracked from In preparation to Signed. Data is sourced from the Sector for Quality and Product Safety of the Ministry of Economy reports. As of 2022, the status is In preparation. The target for 2026 is for the ACCA to be Signed, reflecting an expected progression to finalizing and formally establishing the agreement by the end of the intervention. Signing the ACCA is crucial for enhancing Serbias industrial integration into the EU market, aligning its products with EU standards and thereby simplifying the entry of Serbian industrial goods into the EU market under aligned conformity assessment procedures.

description.narrative: This quantitative indicator measures the annual number of consumer complaints registered and processed in Serbia. A consumer complaint is a formal expression of dissatisfaction made by a consumer regarding a product or service, typically addressed to organizations or regulatory bodies that oversee consumer rights. These complaints are vital metrics for assessing the effectiveness of the consumer protection framework in the country, crucial for aligning Serbian practices with the European Unions standards on consumer rights. Data for this indicator is sourced from the Ministry of Internal and Foreign Trade, confirming its accuracy and relevance. The baseline established in 2022 is 19,027 complaints. The target for 2026 is set at 20,000 complaints, representing an expected increase of approximately 5%. This target is aimed at gauging improvements in the consumer protection system, enhancing the responsiveness and efficiency of authorities in handling consumer issues as part of Serbias broader efforts to integrate into the EU Internal market under Key Area of Intervention 6, Consumer Protection.

Approved: An agreement reaches this status once all relevant parties have formally consented to the terms laid out in the document. Evidence of approval may include the signed agreement, official written confirmations, and published documents or press releases that affirm the agreements acceptance. Implemented: Implementation signifies that the activities outlined in the agreement have been initiated, with resources allocated and actions taken within the agreements framework. description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of actors, encompassing both state and nonstate institutions and organizations, that receive digitalization support through the intervention. Digitalization Support: This encompasses assistance for adopting and implementing digital technologies, tools, and platforms aimed at modernizing operations, enhancing operational efficiency, improving service delivery quality. Support Provided: The assistance could include the delivery of IT equipment, hardware, and software that meet the specific needs of beneficiaries, and the provision of technical assistance and training for the integration into their operational processes and compliance with EU standards, among others. Benefiting Actors: A wide range of actors will benefit from this support, such as public institutions, businesses, citizens, and other stakeholders. Notable beneficiaries will include the Ministry of Internal and Foreign Trade (MIFT), the Intellectual Property Office (IPO), the Commission for the Protection of Competition (CPC), and the Product Service Department (PSD) of the Ministry of Economy. Additionally, sectors like logistics, postal services, financial services, ecommerce aggregators, and micro and smallsized enterprises may also receive support, aiding in the adoption of cashless payments, electronic billing, and other digitalization efforts facilitated by EU4IM.
